# Radoslav Radev Advises Holding Mini Progressions For 6, 7, 8, 9 Seconds, 10 Seconds Between Planche And Front Lever Steps

Radoslav Radev advises using mini progressions between the main planche and front lever steps, and holding a mini progression for 6, 7, 8, 9 seconds, 10 seconds rather than just two seconds. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:21]

## Details

- His advice: to have mini progressions between the progressions, and not just to hold two seconds on the mini progression, but to hold again, let's say, 6, 7, 8, 9 seconds, 10 seconds on the mini progression. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:21]
- For planche: instead of going directly from advanced to straddle planche, use frog, sandwich, rise at legs, pike, half pike, half advanced pike. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:39]
- For front lever: do not go directly from advanced front lever to full front lever; go from advanced to one leg, to one leg on advanced front lever, straddle front lever, baby straddle front lever, full front lever. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 04:00]
- Mini progressions help you feel the muscles and control your body; going directly from tuck to advanced means you cannot feel your muscles or control your body. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:47]
- The smallest thing that can happen from skipping mini progressions is losing protraction or collapsing; the worst is injury. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:53]

## Evidence

- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:21 (Radoslav Radev): "My advice for you, if you want to skip potential injuries, to have mini progressions between the progressions and not just to hold two seconds on the mini progression, but to hold again, let's say, 6, 7, 8, 9 seconds, 10 seconds on the mini progression"
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:30 (Radoslav Radev): "and then the transition will be much easier, and you're not risking that much."
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:39 (Radoslav Radev): "You're not risking to go, for example, from advanced to straddle planche, you're doing frog sandwich rise at legs, pike, half pike, half advanced pike."
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:47 (Radoslav Radev): "it's really good for the activation to feel the muscles, because if you have to go from tuck directly to advanced, you're not feeling your muscles, you can't control your body."
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:53 (Radoslav Radev): "the smallest thing that can happen is just to lose protraction or just collapse. but the worst is injury."
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 04:00 (Radoslav Radev): "On the front lever as well, don't go directly from advanced front lever to full front lever. You can go from advanced to one leg to one leg on advanced front lever, straddle front lever, baby straddle front lever, full front lever."

## Why This Matters

He says mini progressions help you feel the muscles, control your body, and prevent future injuries, and that the transition will be much easier with less risk. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:30]
